response.sql: WITH race_totals AS (SELECT r.name AS race_name, SUM(res.points) AS total_points FROM results res JOIN races r ON r.raceId = res.raceId GROUP BY r.name), kept AS (SELECT race_name, total_points FROM race_totals WHERE total_points > (SELECT AVG(total_points) FROM race_totals)), kept_laps AS (SELECT CAST(res.laps AS REAL) AS laps FROM results res JOIN races r ON r.raceId = res.raceId JOIN kept k ON k.race_name = r.name WHERE res.laps GLOB '[0-9]*') SELECT (SELECT SUM(total_points) FROM kept) AS sum_kept_total_points, (SELECT AVG(laps) FROM kept_laps) AS avg_laps, (SELECT AVG(total_points) FROM kept) - (SELECT AVG(total_points) FROM race_totals) AS avg_excess_over_mean_total

assumptions.assumption: Race names are grouped as plain text, so same-named races from different years or circuits are combined into one race name, as the request specifies.
The threshold is the simple mean of the per-race-name totals, with each race name counting once regardless of how many results it has.
results.laps is stored as text. Only values starting with a digit are kept for the laps average, which excludes NULL and placeholder values such as '\N'. This filter was not checked against the data.
Total points for a race name is the SUM of results.points over all its results, with NULL points ignored by SUM.
